clue.text: When in France I get an awful feeling of envy

parts.note: the French word for I is je
an and a are the same indefinite article
lousy means awful, very poor

explanation.surface: Someone abroad in France is gripped by a horrible pang of envy.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy of another's advantages is the core sense of this emotion, the green-eyed monster.

clue.text: French cleric born in Lincoln

indicators.note: in means the letter for born goes inside the president's short name

parts.note: Abe was the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln, US president
b is the standard abbreviation for born, as in biographies

explanation.surface: A French priest turns out to have been born in the English cathedral city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city but is Abraham Lincoln, ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a priest or clergyman is addressed by this title, so it names a French cleric.

clue.text: Exclude crafty frequenter of pubs

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them
fly is British slang for knowing or crafty

explanation.surface: A landlord bans a sly regular from the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY as an adjective meaning sharp or crafty is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual drinker who hangs about bars is called by this name, a word for a pub regular.

clue.text: Under no obligation to observe established customs?

definitions.text: Under no obligation to observe established customs?

parts.words: Under no obligation to observe established customs?
parts.note: seemingly someone free of traditions, but customs is the border service and the obligation a tax on goods

explanation.surface: A free spirit owes nothing to tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: Customs here is the government department levying import tax, not traditions; goods exempt from that tax carry the label.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods bought without paying customs tax are exempt from the import levy, the obligation in the clue.

clue.text: Hovercraft to transport the police? Right

indicators.note: transport in the sense of carry away, the letters are carried into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the police should use a hovercraft for getting about, met with approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' rearranges THE POLICE into HELICOPTE, then R is added. Hovercraft is a whimsical description: a craft that hovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor aircraft can hang still in the air, so it is literally a craft that hovers.

clue.text: Writer taking tea without cake

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cake goes around the tea

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: An author has his tea but skips the cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. John Buchan was a Scottish novelist who wrote The Thirty-Nine Steps.
explanation.definitionFit: John Buchan was a Scottish novelist, author of The Thirty-Nine Steps, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Coastline seen from quarters on ship

parts.note: south and east are two of the four quarters of the compass
aboard means on a ship

explanation.surface: Sailors view the coast from their cabins on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters looks like cabins but gives two compass points, S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The land along the sea's edge is the seaboard, the coastal region of a country.

clue.text: Dishy redhead turns out to be rather dull

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned around into a different order

parts.note: the head of red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: An attractive red-haired person proves rather boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges DISHY plus R into DRYISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry can mean uninteresting or dull, and the -ish ending softens it to somewhat.

clue.text: Able to help us with fuel product

indicators.note: a product is something made, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A fuel that could help us all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' rearranges FUEL into EFUL, placed after US; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serviceable that can assist is helpful or of use.

clue.text: Colourful source of surprise

definitions.meaning: a colour of the sky, so a colourful word
a surprise comes out of the clear sky, as in the idiom 'out of the ...'

explanation.surface: Something vividly coloured comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Things that come unexpectedly arrive 'out of the blue', so blue is where surprises come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is a colour, and the idiom 'out of the blue' makes the sky the origin of surprises.

clue.text: To get cheaper travel, he avoids paying

definitions.meaning: taking a flight in the dark hours is often cheaper
an unreliable person who slips away from debts, originally by leaving in the dark

explanation.surface: A traveller saves money on fares and dodges the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal, flying at night when fares are cheaper; the second is the noun for a shady customer who flees debts.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated noun names an untrustworthy person who skips off without paying; literally it is to take a night flight.

clue.text: Call for resignation causes uproar

definitions.meaning: a shout of 'out!' demanding someone leave office

explanation.surface: Demands for someone to quit provoke a public storm.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as OUT + CRY, it is literally a cry of 'Out!', the call for a resignation.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public protest is an uproar; split it is a shout of 'out'.

clue.text: Smart girl in the city

parts.note: chic means smart and stylish
Hester is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fashionable young woman out in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Chichester is a cathedral city in West Sussex, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichester is a cathedral city, the county town of West Sussex.

clue.text: German university resentful about French one

indicators.note: about means the word for resentful wraps around the German place

parts.note: sore means aggrieved or resentful
Bonn is a German city with a well-known university

explanation.surface: A German academic institution is bitter about a French rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the German university the subject, but BONN is wordplay and the definition is 'French one', the university in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbonne is the historic university of Paris, so it is a French one.

clue.text: How journalists are recognised and schoolchildren punished

definitions.meaning: the line naming the writer of a newspaper article
pupils punished '...', set to write out sentences

explanation.surface: Reporters get credit while pupils get detention.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines are a school punishment of writing a sentence over and over; split, the answer reads 'by lines'.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles carry the reporter's name in a credit line; children are punished by writing out lines.

clue.text: One who well remembers the penal settlement

indicators.note: settlement here is a new settling of letters, an arrangement into fresh order

explanation.surface: A former convict who recalls the prison colony vividly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' looks like part of 'penal settlement' (a prison colony) but rearranges THE PENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially this animal never forgets, so it is one with a good memory.

clue.text: They get the game off to a flying start

definitions.text: They get the game off to a flying start

parts.words: They get the game off to a flying start
parts.note: sounds like those kicking off a match, but game means birds on a shoot, flushed so they take to the air

explanation.surface: Players who start a match with a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Game is quarry birds, not a match: on a shoot, people walk through cover to drive pheasants into the air for the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: On a shoot these people flush birds from cover, sending the quarry flying.

clue.text: Greek island, one with a colony in Africa at one time

definitions.text: colony in Africa at one time

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Greek island linked to an old African colony.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodesia, named after Cecil Rhodes, was a British colony, now Zambia and Zimbabwe.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was a British colony in southern Africa, now Zambia and Zimbabwe, so a colony of the past.

clue.text: Smiled widely, having support

definitions.meaning: fitted with beams, the timbers that hold a structure up

explanation.surface: Someone grinning broadly because they feel backed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to smile broadly; a beamed ceiling has supporting timbers.

clue.text: Fabric produced only when ready money is shown first

indicators.note: is shown first places the money ahead of the other piece

parts.note: cash is money in hand, ready money
mere means only, nothing more than

explanation.surface: Fine cloth is supplied only when the buyer pays upfront.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, woven into a luxury fabric.

clue.text: One flower in flower

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a dozen'
a bloom is a flower

explanation.surface: A single blossom in full flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant covered in blossom is said to be blooming, that is in flower.

clue.text: Noise in the distance produced by pigs

parts.note: far means at a distance, far away
a row is a noisy din

explanation.surface: A racket heard far off, coming from the pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: A farrow is a litter of piglets, what a sow produces; as a verb it means to give birth to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrow is a litter of piglets, the young that a sow brings forth.

clue.text: A softer sort of wood

indicators.note: sort here works as a verb meaning arrange, so the letters are sorted again

explanation.surface: A variety of timber that is less hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges SOFTER into the answer; 'A softer sort of wood' reads as softwood.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is a tract of trees, and forest is a larger version of it.

clue.text: Rebel MP has reformed, so he swears!

indicators.note: a reformed character is changed, so these letters are re-formed into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebellious politician reforms, so he insists by solemn oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges REBEL MP HAS. 'Swears' seems to mean takes an oath; it means uses profane language.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who curses using sacred names profanely is one who swears.

clue.text: Do a turn at the helm, perhaps

definitions.text: Do a turn at the helm, perhaps

parts.words: Do a turn at the helm, perhaps
parts.note: reads as taking a spell of duty steering, but means changing direction, as a helmsman may

explanation.surface: Taking one's shift steering the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do a turn' suggests a stint at the wheel; it actually means to swing round onto a new course.
explanation.definitionFit: To change course or swing round is to turn, which a ship does at the helmsman's hand.

clue.text: In truth she is head of a big place

definitions.text: In truth she is head of a big place

parts.words: In truth she is head of a big place
parts.note: a girl's name meaning true in Latin, which also starts the name of a Mexican city whose name means True Cross

explanation.surface: Honestly, the woman runs a large establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Veracruz is a major Mexican port whose name means True Cross: the first part is Latin for true and also a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is Latin for true and a woman's name, and it heads the Mexican city name meaning True Cross.

clue.text: Control earth's gravity above the pole

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to Earth's gravity
over means above
N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: Gravity pulls everything down toward the pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule or have control over something.

clue.text: Absent-minded girl's distinguishing feature

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and the possessive gives an S
a trait is a distinguishing characteristic

explanation.surface: A young woman whose defining quality is her forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word describes someone distracted or preoccupied.
